stem: What is the median of these five tempos?
stimulus: Tempos of five pieces of music, in beats per minute: 72, 116, 84, 120, 88
explanation: Sort the values first: 72, 84, 88, 116, 120. There are five values, so the median is the third one, 88. Use this whenever an SAT question gives a short list and asks for the median. If you skip the sort, you will get these questions wrong even when the arithmetic is easy.

A.why: You found the range, 120 − 72 = 48. The range measures spread, not the middle value.

B.why: You took the middle entry of the list as it was written, without sorting it. 84 sits in the middle of the unsorted list, but it is the second-smallest value.

D.why: You found the mean, 480 ÷ 5 = 96. The question asks for the median, which is the middle value after sorting.

stem: What is the mean number of lanes per street?
stimulus:
Lanes per Street on 10 City Streets
Number of lanes | Number of streets
2 | 6
3 | 3
4 | 1
explanation: Weight each lane count by how many streets have it: $2(6) + 3(3) + 4(1) = 12 + 9 + 4 = 25$ lanes in total. There are $6 + 3 + 1 = 10$ streets, so the mean is $25 \div 10 = 2.5$. Any SAT question that asks for a mean from a frequency table works this way.

A.why: You found the median. The 5th and 6th of the 10 streets both have 2 lanes, so the median is 2, but the question asks for the mean.

C.why: You averaged the three lane values, (2 + 3 + 4) ÷ 3 = 3, without weighting them by frequency. Six streets have 2 lanes, so 2 should count six times.

D.why: You found the total number of lanes, 25, but did not divide by the 10 streets.

stem: What is the median of these six lengths?
stimulus: Lengths of six fossil leaves, in millimeters: 14, 9, 25, 17, 11, 20
explanation: Sort the values: 9, 11, 14, 17, 20, 25. With six values there are two middle values, 14 and 17, so the median is their average: $(14 + 17) \div 2 = 15.5$ mm. SAT questions that ask for the median of an even-sized set work this way.

A.why: You sorted correctly but took only the lower of the two middle values. When the count is even, you average the two middle values.

C.why: You found the mean, 96 ÷ 6 = 16. The question asks for the median.

D.why: You averaged the two middle entries of the unsorted list, 25 and 17. Sort the list before you look for the middle.

stem: What is the mean of these five counts?
stimulus: Meteors counted in each of five hours: 10, 18, 6, 13, 28
explanation: Add the values: $10 + 18 + 6 + 13 + 28 = 75$. There are five values, so the mean is $75 \div 5 = 15$ meteors. SAT questions that ask for the mean of a list work this way, and so do questions about how adding or removing a value changes the mean.

A.why: You took the middle entry of the unsorted list. That is neither the mean nor the median. It is actually the smallest value.

B.why: You found the median. Sorted, the list is 6, 10, 13, 18, 28, and the middle value is 13. The question asks for the mean.

D.why: You found the range, 28 − 6 = 22. That measures spread, not center.
